Perth-based, ASX-listed battery materials company developing graphite anode production in Sweden, with its Vittangi graphite mine in the north and a planned Luleå anode refinery producing Talnode materials for lithium-ion batteries, aimed at European gigafactories and automakers. It also sells Talphite graphene-style additives. Still pre-commercial, with offtake agreements with customers such as Mitsubishi and European carmakers. B2B with little consumer profile outside investor circles.

Canadian potash developer in Saskatchewan, focused on the Milestone solution-mining project near Regina, aiming to supply fertiliser potash to farmers and distributors in North America and export markets. It was TSX Venture listed, pre-production and reliant on equity and project financing, and later restructured as Western Resources. B2B mining developer with no consumer brand and no meaningful operating revenue to date. Potash is a crop nutrient, and the Milestone project was designed as a long-life solution mine, with value tied to fertiliser prices and project financing.

Texas-based holding company, formerly Ecoark, listed on Nasdaq (ZEST), whose businesses included Zest Labs freshness-management software for fresh food supply chains used with Walmart, the Banner Midstream oil and gas assets and trading and fintech holdings. It was later renamed BitNile Metaverse and pivoted to metaverse and crypto-related ventures under Ault Alliance's influence. Customers were retailers, growers and energy buyers. Small cap, with little consumer brand profile.

Vancouver-based, TSX Venture listed exploration company whose flagship is the Johnson Tract polymetallic project in Alaska, a gold, copper and zinc volcanogenic massive sulphide deposit near Cook Inlet, held in partnership with the Alaska Native regional corporation Cook Inlet Region, Inc. It is a pre-revenue developer funding drilling programmes, resource updates and early economic studies through equity raises from mining investors. B2B junior miner with no consumer profile.

Perth-based gold developer listed on the ASX (ORR) with the Nyanzaga gold project in Tanzania's Lake Victoria goldfields as its main asset, which was being studied for open-pit development. It was acquired by Perseus Mining in 2023 following a takeover contest. Pre-production, so revenue was nil, and customers would have been gold refiners. B2B resource company with no consumer brand.

Perth-based ASX-listed gold miner (PNR) operating the Norseman Gold Project in the Eastern Goldfields of Western Australia, which it took over in a 2022 joint venture, and the Halls Creek project in the Kimberley. Output is sold to refiners as bullion and has been in the range of 100,000 ounces a year, with several hundred employees on site. Small to mid-cap producer, B2B with no consumer profile.

Brisbane-based, ASX-listed coking coal developer and producer in Queensland's Bowen Basin, owning the Burton open-cut complex and the Isaac Plains area projects, producing steelmaking coal sold to Asian steel mills in India, Japan and South Korea. It is a mid-sized junior with heavy financing pressure when metallurgical coal prices fell. Customers are steelmakers and traders, so it is B2B mining with no consumer profile.

Perth-based lithium explorer-developer listed on the ASX (DLI), with the Mt Ida project in Western Australia and the Yinnetharra project in the Gascoyne region, both focused on spodumene hard rock lithium for battery makers. It is pre-revenue, funding drilling and studies through equity raises. B2B resource company with no consumer visibility. Lithium demand comes from electric vehicle batteries, so value depends on spodumene prices and on offtake or processing partnerships.

Perth-based ASX-listed (NTU) rare earths company developing the Browns Range project in Western Australia's Kimberley, targeting dysprosium and terbium, heavy rare earths used in permanent magnets for electric vehicles and wind turbines. It has offtake agreements with Iluka and other partners and is largely pre-revenue. B2B with little consumer awareness. Customers are Asian processors and magnet makers, so the company has no consumer profile, although the critical minerals theme gets government support.

Botswana copper and silver mining company operating the Khoemacau mine in the Kalahari copper belt, with production of about 40,000 tonnes of copper a year. MMG, a Chinese-controlled miner, acquired it in 2023. Customers are smelters and traders. B2B and no consumer profile. Khoemacau was a standalone company before the sale, with mines near Maun and Ghanzi in north-western Botswana, and a large mineral resource.
cb_desc: Khoemacau Copper Mining is a copper-silver mining company.

about: West African gold producer headquartered in the UK with operations in Mali and Guinea. Owned and operated the Yanfolila gold mine in Mali, developed the Kouroussa project in Guinea, and was listed on London's AIM (HUM) and the Toronto exchange before being acquired by Nioko Resources in 2024. Sells gold bullion to refiners. Mid-tier mining producer producing around 100,000 ounces a year, with no consumer profile.

South Korean battery materials maker producing electrolytic copper foil used in lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles and electronics. Customers are battery cell makers such as SK On and LG Energy Solution. Was an affiliate of the Iljin group and was acquired by Lotte Chemical in 2021, later renamed Lotte Energy Materials, expanding capacity in Korea, Malaysia and Hungary. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer profile.

about: US producer of titanium and specialty metals, headquartered in Pittsburgh and listed on the NYSE (RTI) before its acquisition. Made titanium mill products, extrusions and fabricated parts for aerospace, defence, medical and industrial customers. Acquired by Alcoa in 2015 for about 1.5 billion USD and integrated into its aerospace business, which later became part of Arconic and Howmet. B2B supplier with no consumer profile.

about: Canadian gold producer listed on the TSX and NYSE (AGI), operating mines including Young-Davidson and Island Gold in Ontario, Mulatos in Mexico, and Kirazlı in Turkey, with the Lynx and Magino projects added. Produces roughly 500,000 ounces of gold a year. Revenue is gold bullion sold to refiners and banks. Mid-tier miner with strong investor recognition and no consumer brand profile.

Gold mining company that owns the Asanko Gold Mine in Ghana's Ashanti region, a producer with several open pits and a processing plant of about five million tonnes a year, listed on the TSX and NYSE American (GAU). Formerly Asanko Gold, it was renamed Galiano Gold in 2020 and focused on mine life extension and exploration. Produces gold doré sold to refiners under offtake arrangements, mostly in Ghana. Mid-sized miner with no consumer profile.

Chinese online steel trading platform (Zhaogang) founded in 2012 in Shanghai. Buyers and sellers trade steel products through its website and app, while it adds logistics, warehousing, financing, processing and data services to speed up delivery. Revenue comes from product sales and service fees. Customers are steel mills, traders and construction or manufacturing buyers. Backed by investors including Tiger Global, Hillhouse and Goldman Sachs. B2B brand known in Chinese industrial circles with no consumer profile.

about: Lithium chemicals producer formed in January 2024 by the merger of Livent and Allkem, listed on the NYSE (ALTM). Produced lithium hydroxide and carbonate from brine in Argentina's Salar del Hombre Muerto and hard-rock sources in Australia and Canada, selling to battery and cathode makers. Acquired by Rio Tinto in 2025 for about 6.7 billion USD. B2B materials supplier with no consumer profile.

Canadian gold producer that developed the Moose River Consolidated gold mine in Nova Scotia, a large open-pit operation built to produce around 100,000 ounces a year, plus nearby development projects such as Beaver Dam, and was listed on the TSX. It sold gold doré to refiners and had a mainly Atlantic Canada footprint. Acquired by Australia's St Barbara in 2019 for about 722 million Canadian dollars. B2B mining company with no consumer profile.

Development-stage miner with no revenue and no consumer profile.

about: Gold producer listed on the ASX, London and Johannesburg (RSG), with operations including the Syama mine in Mali, the Mako mine in Senegal, the Bibiani mine in Ghana, and the Ravenswood project in Queensland. Produces around 350,000 to 400,000 ounces of gold a year and sells to refiners. More than 25 years of operating history. Mid-tier miner with no consumer profile, though known to investors and in West African mining.

Canadian copper miner that operated the Copper Mountain mine near Princeton, British Columbia, producing copper concentrate with gold and silver by-products, with expansion plans and a stake in the Eva copper project in Queensland. Sells concentrate to smelters under offtake contracts. Was listed on the TSX and ASX and was acquired by Hudbay Minerals in 2023 for about 439 million Canadian dollars. B2B miner with no consumer profile.

Canadian gold and copper mining company, listed on the TSX, with operations in Bulgaria (Chelopech and Ada Tepe) and a copper smelter in Namibia (Tsumeb), plus exploration in Serbia and Ecuador. Previously Dundee Precious Metals, it renamed to DPM Metals. Sells gold and copper concentrate to smelters and traders and produces roughly 250,000 ounces of gold a year. Mid-tier miner with strong investor following and no consumer profile.

about: Australian gold miner listed on the ASX (VAU), formed from the merger of Red 5 and Silver Lake Resources, and renamed Vault Minerals. Operates the Deflector copper-gold mine, King of the Hills and Mount Monger operations in Western Australia, plus the Sugar Zone mine in Canada. Sells gold and copper concentrate to refiners and smelters. Mid-tier producer with a well-established investor following, but no consumer brand profile.

Canadian mineral exploration company focused on zinc, lead and silver, holding the Cirque project in northeastern British Columbia, a large undeveloped deposit that was historically explored by larger miners. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. As an explorer it does not sell products, and funds drilling and studies through share sales to investors. Small resource company with no consumer profile and attention mostly from junior-mining investors.

Canadian-based gold and antimony miner, listed on the TSX (MND), operating the Costerfield mine in Victoria, Australia, which is one of the world's few antimony-producing mines, and the Bjorkdal gold mine in Sweden. Sells gold and antimony concentrate to smelters and refiners. Annual gold-equivalent production is roughly 100,000 ounces. Mid-tier miner with no consumer brand profile, though antimony supply has drawn attention from investors.

Australian nickel producer listed on the ASX, which owned the Kambalda nickel operations in Western Australia, including the Cassini and Northern Operations underground mines, and sold nickel concentrate to smelters, positioning itself for electric vehicle battery metals demand. Acquired by Wyloo Metals, the investment arm of Andrew Forrest, in 2022 and then delisted. Mid-sized miner with no consumer profile, known mostly to resource investors and traders in the nickel market.

Canadian gold exploration and development company focused on Namibia, where it advanced the Twin Hills project and other gold projects in the Karibib region, one of the country's emerging gold districts. Acquired by Yintai Gold in 2024. As an explorer and developer it had no sales and raised funds from investors, with a feasibility study and plans for an open-pit mine. Small resource company with no consumer profile.

Australian lithium exploration and development company focused on the Paradox Basin in Utah, where it holds brine and mineral rights over large areas and has tested direct lithium extraction. Listed on the ASX and based in Perth. It aims to produce lithium carbonate for EV batteries, financing studies and pilot plants through share sales and partners. Early-stage resource company with no consumer profile, followed mainly by lithium investors.

Australian potash developer, listed on the ASX, advancing the Beyond Potash project (formerly Lake Wells and Lake Disappointment) in Western Australia to produce sulphate of potash fertiliser for Australian and Asian farmers. The company has no revenue and is financed by investors and government support. Based in Perth. Early-stage resource company with no consumer profile and attention mainly from agricultural-minerals investors.

Canadian gold exploration company that discovered the Oko West gold deposit in Guyana, a high-grade project in the Guiana Shield that drew interest from major miners and was advanced through drilling and economic studies. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and based in Quebec. Funds work via share sales and has no production. Early-stage resource company with no consumer profile, but well known to gold investors.

Australian uranium developer, listed on the ASX (VMY), focused on the Mulga Rock project in Western Australia, an undeveloped deposit intended to supply nuclear power plants worldwide. It has no production and raises money from investors, and has pursued approvals and offtake discussions with utilities in Asia and elsewhere. Based in Perth. Small resource company with no consumer profile, followed by uranium investors and specialist funds.

Northgate Minerals was a Vancouver-based mid-tier gold and copper producer that ran the Kemess mine in northern British Columbia and held the Young-Davidson gold project in Ontario. It sold gold-copper concentrate to smelters and gold to refiners. The company was listed on the Toronto and NYSE American exchanges and was acquired by AuRico Gold in 2011. Resource company with no consumer brand, now defunct as an independent firm.

about: SEMAFO was a Canadian gold mining company operating in West Africa, with the Mana mine and Boungou mine in Burkina Faso and exploration in Guinea and elsewhere, producing roughly 250,000 ounces of gold a year at its peak. It was headquartered in Saint-Laurent, Quebec, and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and Stockholm exchange. Endeavour Mining acquired it in 2020 in an all-share transaction. Resource producer with no consumer brand.

Heron Resources is an Australian base-metals company that developed the Woodlawn zinc-copper mine in New South Wales, reprocessing tailings and mining underground to supply zinc and copper concentrates and lead to smelters. It was based in Sydney and listed on the ASX and Toronto Stock Exchange, then entered administration in 2022 and was acquired by Develop Global. Resource company with no consumer brand visibility.

about: Klondex Mines was a gold and silver producer with high-grade underground operations in Nevada (Fire Creek and Midas) and the True North mine in Manitoba, Canada. Its operations were based in Reno, Nevada, and it sold gold concentrate and doré to smelters. Hecla Mining acquired the company in 2018 for around $462 million. Resource producer with no consumer brand and now part of Hecla.

Roxgold was a Toronto-based gold miner that operated the Yaramoko mine in Burkina Faso and held exploration licences in Cote d'Ivoire, producing about 100,000-plus ounces annually. It listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and sold gold to refiners. Fortuna Silver Mines acquired it in 2021 in a deal valued at about C$1.5 billion. Resource company without consumer visibility. Burkina Faso was its only producing country.

Australian Potash is an exploration and development company based in Subiaco, Western Australia and listed on the ASX, working on the Lake Wells sulphate of potash project, a salt-lake brine resource in the Goldfields region that could supply fertiliser to Australian and Asian farmers. It has no revenue yet. Junior resources company with no consumer brand. Fertiliser buyers in Asia would be the intended customers, shipping through Western Australian ports.

Great Panther Mining was a Vancouver-based precious metals miner that operated silver and gold mines in Mexico and Brazil and sold concentrate and doré. It was listed on the Toronto and NYSE American exchanges. Resource producer with no consumer brand. Its operations included the Topia and Guanajuato silver-gold mines in Mexico and the Tucano gold mine in Brazil, selling concentrate and doré to smelters and refiners.

MAG Silver is a Vancouver-based exploration and development company whose major asset is a 44% interest in the Juanicipio silver-gold mine in Zacatecas, Mexico, which it holds with operator Fresnillo plc. Pan American Silver agreed to acquire it in 2025 in a deal valued at about $2.1 billion. It was listed on the TSX and NYSE American. Resource company without consumer brand profile.

Auryn Resources is a Toronto-based gold exploration company that held projects in Canada's Nunavut territory (Committee Bay) and in Peru, listed on the TSX and NYSE American. It had no production and relied on equity raising to fund drilling. Junior mining explorer with no consumer brand profile. Exploration spending is funded through share issues and partnerships rather than sales. It has no producing mines.

AVZ Minerals is an Australian-listed explorer based in Perth that holds the Manono lithium and tin project in the Democratic Republic of Congo, regarded as one of the world's largest hard-rock lithium deposits. It has been in a prolonged legal dispute with state miner Cominiere and Chinese group Zijin Mining over ownership rights. It has no revenue. Resource developer with no consumer brand.

Corsa Coal is a mining company that produced metallurgical coal for steelmakers from mines in Pennsylvania and Maryland, Northern Appalachia, and exported to customers in Europe, Asia and Brazil. It was listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and run from Canonsburg, Pennsylvania. It is B2B commodity producer with no consumer visibility. Its coal is used in steelmaking, sold to blast furnace and coke makers rather than power stations.
